citation: Han JM, Sahin M. TSC1/TSC2 signaling in the CNS. FEBS Letters. 2011. doi:10.1016/j.febslet.2011.02.001. PMID:21329690.
description: Reviews the TSC1/TSC2 complex as a conserved negative regulator of mTORC1 and summarizes CNS consequences of TSC loss. This supports interpreting Tsc1 and Tsc2 perturbations as mTORC1-activating loss-of-function perturbations.

citation: Schuele M, Butto T, Dewi S, Schlichtholz L, Strand S, Gerber S, Endres K, Schweiger S, Winter J. mTOR Driven Gene Transcription Is Required for Cholesterol Production in Neurons of the Developing Cerebral Cortex. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2021. doi:10.3390/ijms22116034. PMID:34204880.
description: Shows that mTORC1 regulates sterol and cholesterol biosynthesis gene transcription in primary neurons and developing mouse cortex. It connects TSC loss through mTORC1 to increased sterol-pathway transcripts such as Cyp51, Hmgcs1, Insig1, Ldlr, and Msmo1.

citation: Alesi N, Akl EW, Khabibullin D, Liu HJ, Nidhiry AS, Garner ER, Filippakis H, Lam HC, Shi W, Viswanathan SR, Morroni M, Ferguson SM, Henske EP. TSC2 regulates lysosome biogenesis via a non-canonical RAGC and TFEB-dependent mechanism. Nature Communications. 2021. doi:10.1038/s41467-021-24499-6. PMID:34253722.
description: Demonstrates that TSC1/2-deficient cells and Tsc2 mutant tissues increase lysosome biogenesis through TFEB. This supports Tsc1/Tsc2 loss producing increased lysosomal transcripts such as Atp6v0b and Lamp2.

citation: Katoh M. Multi-layered prevention and treatment of chronic inflammation, organ fibrosis and cancer associated with canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling activation. International Journal of Molecular Medicine. 2018. doi:10.3892/ijmm.2018.3689. PMID:29786110.
description: Summarizes APC as a negative regulator in the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin pathway and lists AXIN2 and NKD1 as representative beta-catenin targets. This supports increased Axin2/Nkd1 after Apc loss as a direct Wnt de-repression response.

citation: Liu XH, Zhang ZY, Andersson KB, Husberg C, Enger UH, Raeder MG, Christensen G, Louch WE. Cardiomyocyte-specific disruption of Serca2 in adult mice causes sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis. Cell Calcium. 2010. doi:10.1016/j.ceca.2010.09.009. PMID:20965565.
description: Reports that adult mouse Serca2 disruption induces the unfolded-protein response, PERK/eIF2-alpha signaling, CHOP, and apoptosis. This directly predicts increased ER-stress transcripts after Atp2a2 loss.

citation: Poche RA, Zhang M, Rueda EM, Tong X, McElwee ML, Wong L, Hsu CW, Dejosez M, Burns AR, Fox DA, Martin JF, Zwaka TP, Dickinson ME. RONIN Is an Essential Transcriptional Regulator of Genes Required for Mitochondrial Function in the Developing Retina. Cell Reports. 2016. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2016.01.039. PMID:26876175.
description: Shows that THAP11/RONIN positively regulates a cohort of mitochondrial genes, including electron-transport-chain genes, and that Ronin loss reduces ETC activity. This supports decreased mitochondrial transcripts after Thap11 perturbation.

citation: Potting C, Crochemore C, Moretti F, Nigsch F, Schmidt I, Manneville C, Carbone W, Knehr J, DeJesus R, Lindeman A, Maher R, Russ C, McAllister G, Reece-Hoyes JS, Hoffman GR, Roma G, Muller M, Sailer AW, Helliwell SB. Genome-wide CRISPR screen for PARKIN regulators reveals transcriptional repression as a determinant of mitophagy. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2017. doi:10.1073/pnas.1711023115. PMID:29269392.
description: Identifies THAP11 as a transcriptional repressor of PARKIN and shows that THAP11 CRISPR knockout increases PARKIN in several cell types, including human iPSC-derived neurons. This directly supports increased Prkn after Thap11 loss.

citation: Waszak SM, Robinson GW, Gudenas BL, Smith KS, Forget A, Kojic M, Garcia-Lopez J, Hadley J, Hamilton KV, Indersie E, Buchhalter I, Kerssemakers J, Jager N, Sharma T, Rausch T, Kool M, Sturm D, Jones DTW, Vasilyeva A, Tatevossian RG, Neale G, Lombard B, Loew D, Nakitandwe J, Rusch M, Bowers DC, Bendel A, Partap S, Chintagumpala M, Crawford J, Gottardo NG, Smith A, Dufour C, Rutkowski S, Eggen T, Wesenberg F, Kjaerheim K, Feychting M, Lannering B, Schutz J, Johansen C, Andersen TV, Roosli M, Kuehni CE, Grotzer M, Remke M, Puget S, Pajtler KW, Milde T, Witt O, Ryzhova M, Korshunov A, Orr BA, Ellison DW, Brugieres L, Lichter P, Nichols KE, Gajjar A, Wainwright BJ, Ayrault O, Korbel JO, Northcott PA, Pfister SM. Germline Elongator mutations in Sonic Hedgehog medulloblastoma. Nature. 2020. doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2164-5. PMID:32296180.
description: Links ELP1 loss to destabilization of the Elongator complex, loss of wobble uridine tRNA modifications, translational reprogramming, and induction of the unfolded-protein response in Sonic Hedgehog medulloblastoma. This supports ER/UPR transcripts after Elp1 loss and supplies a complex-level bridge for Elp2.

citation: Zhang R, Farshadyeganeh P, Ohkawara B, Nakajima K, Takeda JI, Ito M, Zhang S, Miyasaka Y, Ohno T, Mori-Yoshimura M, Masuda A, Ohno K. Muscle-specific lack of Gfpt1 triggers ER stress to alleviate misfolded protein accumulation. Disease Models & Mechanisms. 2024. doi:10.1242/dmm.050768. PMID:38903011.
description: Shows that muscle-specific Gfpt1 deficiency and Gfpt1-silenced myotubes have reduced O-GlcNAcylation with elevated unfolded-protein-response markers. This predicts ER/UPR up-regulation after Gfpt1 loss.

citation: Tognon E, Kobia F, Busi I, Fumagalli A, De Masi F, Vaccari T. Control of lysosomal biogenesis and Notch-dependent tissue patterning by components of the TFEB-V-ATPase axis in Drosophila melanogaster. Autophagy. 2016. doi:10.1080/15548627.2015.1134080. PMID:26727288.
description: Connects V-ATPase subunits, including the ATP6V0C ortholog, to endolysosomal function and TFEB/Mitf-regulated lysosomal biogenesis. It is a mechanistic but cross-species bridge for Atp6v0c responses involving Atp6v0a1 and endolysosomal genes.

citation: Kunselman JM, Williamson CD, Golding AE, Jia R, Sohn M, Dale RK, Bonifacino JS. The hereditary spastic paraplegia type 21 (SPG21) protein is a RAB7A effector that promotes noncanonical mTORC1-catalyzed TFEB phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention. Molecular Biology of the Cell. 2025. doi:10.1091/mbc.E25-07-0346. PMID:40833810.
description: Places GTP-bound RAB7A at endolysosomes upstream of a noncanonical mTORC1-TFEB phosphorylation route through the SPG21 effector. This provides an indirect bridge from Rab7 perturbation to lysosomal/TFEB transcriptional changes.
